pages.text: "I will not eat this green." Timid Lala pushed at one section of the plate with a finger. Lunch stood on the long window table. Each section had a different color. An unfamiliar side dish filled the green section.
Lala wanted to run longest in the yard that afternoon. But sniffing the green made their shoulders hunch. The spoon stopped before that section.
Impatient Bobo took a green bite and called loudly, "This is so delicious!" Lala covered both ears. Only the green section remained heaped on Lala's plate.
After lunch, everyone went outside. Tag began. Lala ran happily too, but Bobo was already far ahead.
Soon, Lala's feet kept slowing. "Oh? Why are my legs so heavy...?" Lala plopped in the shade, fiddling with a purple hair clip.
Even after two laps of the yard, Bobo ran fast. "I ate five colors today! Five colors on my plate—yum!" Lala could only watch from the shade.
At lunch the next day, the green section appeared again. Lala's hands curled. "Green... again."
Teacher Bau sat beside Lala and gently pointed at the plate. "Green is a color that gives your legs strength. All five colors help you run longer." Lala stared at the green section.
Lala brought green close to their nose, then took a crunchy bite. "Oh? Not scary! One, a white bite! Two, a yellow bite! Three, a green bite too!" Five colors on my plate—yum! The plate was empty.

That afternoon, Lala ran through the whole game of tag. Teacher Bau cradled Lala's cheeks in both hands. Eating all five colors left strength in those legs. "Bobo, five colors tomorrow too! Five colors on my plate—yum!"
